bullets.title: S&P 500 crosses 7,600 for first time; software up 14% in 3 days, best run since 2001
bullets.body: The S&P 500 hit 7,600 for the first time (up 29% YoY, 81% 5-year), closing +0.26% on the session while the Nasdaq added 0.42%. Software ETF IGV surged ~16% over 3 sessions — its best 3-day run in ~25 years — driven by short covering and positioning unwinds, outperforming semis for the 4th straight session. Goldman's TMT desk notes software outperformed the S&P 500 by >1,000bps over two days, the largest such stretch in ~25 years.

bullets.title: May ISM Manufacturing hits 54.0, 4-year high; JPM upgrades Q2 GDP forecast to 2.5%
bullets.body: The May ISM Manufacturing PMI came in at 54.0 vs. 53.0 consensus (prior 52.7), the highest reading since May 2022, with new orders surging to 56.8 and employment rising to 48.6. The S&P Global final PMI was 55.1, the 10th consecutive month above 50. JPMorgan's Feroli upgraded his Q2 2026 GDP forecast from 2.0% to 2.5% on the print; the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model stands at 3.0% (down from 3.8%).

bullets.title: Alphabet launches $80B equity raise — largest since Aramco — to fund AI infrastructure
bullets.body: Alphabet announced a total $80B equity capital raise: $15B mandatory convertible preferred, $15B common stock (pricing June 2), $40B ATM program starting Q3 2026, and a $10B private placement with Berkshire Hathaway at $351.81/share (Class A) and $348.20/share (Class C). Proceeds earmarked for AI compute infrastructure and global capex. Transaction is covered with aggregate demand exceeding offering amount.

bullets.title: NVDA +6% on Vera Rubin production ramp and RTX Spark PC launch; ARM +12-15% on Barclays PT hike to $360
bullets.body: NVIDIA entered full production on Vera Rubin, its multi-rack agentic AI platform (NVL72), and launched RTX Spark — an ARM-based Grace CPU + Blackwell GPU system for PCs co-developed with MSFT — into 30+ laptops and 10 desktops from Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo targeting fall 2026. Barclays raised ARM's price target to $360 from $250; ARM shares surged 12-15% with the stock having rallied from $134 to $413 in 2.5 months. QCOM sank 7.6% and INTC fell 6.7% at open on competitive threat.

bullets.title: Oil surges 5%+ as Iran halts US talks, threatens Strait of Hormuz closure; Trump dismisses oil concerns
bullets.body: WTI crude rose 5.79% to $92.42 and Brent surged to ~$96/bbl after Iran halted indirect US negotiations citing Israeli operations in Lebanon/Gaza, with Iran's foreign ministry threatening to 'completely block' the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said he 'doesn't care' if talks are over, pledged to maintain the blockade, and predicted oil prices will fall 'like a rock' — a later Hezbollah ceasefire announcement trimmed oil gains. A cargo ship was struck by what Iraqi authorities assessed as a drone ~40 miles southeast of Umm Qasr.

bullets.title: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire announced; SPX staged afternoon reversal on Trump Truth Social post
bullets.body: Trump announced a ceasefire agreement with Hezbollah — Israel agreed to halt shooting, no US soldiers will head to Beirut, and forces en route were recalled — after a call with Netanyahu and senior envoys. The SPX staged an intraday reversal on the headline. Iran separately warned that ceasefire violations on one front equal violations on all fronts, and Iran's foreign ministry blamed the US for ceasefire violations.

bullets.title: Anthropic confidentially files draft S-1; Polymarket prices 76% odds it IPOs before OpenAI
bullets.body: Anthropic submitted a confidential draft S-1 registration statement to the SEC for a proposed IPO of common stock. The filing is a bullish read-through for AI infrastructure suppliers per some buyside commentary. Polymarket prices a 76% probability Anthropic goes public before OpenAI. Salesforce's Anthropic investment is reportedly valued at ~$5B.

bullets.title: Front-end Treasury yields back off 4% resistance; JPM sees path to mid-3.80s
bullets.body: The 2-year Treasury yield backed up to 3.98-4.02% before fading; JPMorgan's rates desk sees a close richer than 3.98% confirming a trend reversal to the 3.895% 50-day moving average and then mid-3.80s by mid-summer. The 10-year finished +0.4bps at 4.457%, well below the intraday high. Treasury 2Y closed at 4.035% (+2.1bps) as Middle East tensions initially pushed front-end higher before Trump negotiation signals pulled yields back.

bullets.title: Goldman warns market is 'more convicted, concentrated, and levered' in AI; structurally elevated volatility
bullets.body: Goldman's 1-Delta desk and a top Goldman trader flagged that the AI trade has shifted from quality fundamentals to leverage and speculation — echoing the 'next SK Hynix' hunt — while the market overall is 'uncomfortably concentrated.' Call option volume on IGV hit a record 280k contracts Friday followed by 225k Monday. GS cautions that Cyclicals vs Defensives pairs are at all-time highs following sharp rallies in Airlines (+19.1%), Retailers (+10.2%), and Homebuilders (+6.6%) since May 15, suggesting exposure reduction.

bullets.title: Utilities sector -3% as CEG prices $281 share offering; renewables weak; power demand regulation tightens
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Utilities Index fell 3%, Electric Utilities -3.4%, with CEG down 7.7% after pricing an 11M share offering at $281. ENPH -6.8%, BE -4.1%, and the solar ETF -3.8%. Separately, Texas's Hill County passed the state's first datacenter moratorium in May 2026 and Pennsylvania introduced mandatory datacenter power payment legislation (H.B. 1834), signaling a broader regulatory shift that could create headwinds for datacenter build-out economics.

bullets.title: UBS sees current AI bubble analogous to late 1998, not Q1 2000; $7.8tn money market wall as potential fuel
bullets.body: UBS Asia feedback notes all 7 bubble preconditions are present but conditions resemble late 1998/early 1999 rather than peak Q1 2000, with $7.8tn in money market funds (60% above inflation-adjusted average) implying $2.4tn in potential equity inflows. Goldman's unprofitable tech basket gained 27% in May vs. Nasdaq 100's +10%, the widest outperformance since November 2020, while non-profitable Russell 2000 stocks continue to outperform profitable peers YTD.

bullets.title: ECB June 25bp hike fully priced for first time since May 4; Eurozone input prices surging
bullets.body: Traders now fully price a 25bp ECB rate hike in June for the first time since May 4. Eurozone manufacturing input and output prices rose at their fastest pace in May, adding to European inflation concerns even as the DAX fell 0.44% and FTSE 100 fell 0.82% on the session.

bullets.title: MRVL likely added to S&P 500 on June 5 per quant handicappers; S&P rule change reduces profitability bar
bullets.body: Quant models flag MRVL as the #1 candidate for S&P 500 addition on June 5 (announcement expected at 5:15pm EDT), with SOFI and VRT also ranking highly. Separately, S&P 500 changed its inclusion rules to no longer require profitability and reduced the cooldown period from 12 to 6 months, a change that could trigger ~$31B in passive forced buying for qualifying names.

bullets.title: JPM rates desk: JOLTS expected near 6.9mn; NFP Friday is the key macro event of the week
bullets.body: JPMorgan projects JOLTS job openings to tick up slightly to 6.900mn (consensus 6.866mn), leaving the job openings rate stable at 4.1% with early stabilization signals from Indeed. Morgan Stanley forecasts Friday's NFP at +65k total / +75k private with unemployment steady at 4.3% and wages at +3.4% YoY, with airline bankruptcies and CDL law changes creating ~20k drag.

bullets.title: Money market fund assets hit record $8.28tn; S&P 500 earnings growth forecast at 24% — highest outside recessions
bullets.body: Money market fund AUM reached a record $8.28 trillion. Separately, S&P 500 earnings are expected to grow 24% this year — a level not seen outside post-recessionary rebounds — driven by mega-cap tech EPS gains. The S&P 500's rally since late April is characterized by one strategist as 'healthy and fueled by AI visibility and 1Q26 EPS upside of $10.'

bullets.title: TSMC foundry revenue hits record $48.8B in 1Q26 (+32% y/y); N3 node remains AI supply bottleneck
bullets.body: Global foundry industry revenue hit a record $48.8B in 1Q26, +32% y/y and the 9th consecutive quarter of growth; 2Q26E projects $54.7B (+29% y/y). TSMC's market share widened to 95%+, posted +41% y/y growth with record margins, and its Arizona Phase 1 quarterly net profit in 1Q26 alone exceeded all of CY25. N3 remains the primary supply bottleneck of the AI cycle.

bullets.title: Sector rotation update: Big Tech underperforms; Mag7 lagged despite no clear negative theme
bullets.body: On the day, AMZN fell 3.5-4.5%, META fell 5.1-5.5%, and GOOGL fell 1%, while NVDA gained 6%, MSFT gained 2.8% to a 4-month high, and AVGO/MSFT each gained ~8% over two days. JPM notes Momentum factor fell 3.3% (-1.9 sigma) and advises reducing Cyclicals exposure after the May 15-29 rally. Software and cybersecurity led within Nasdaq; GS Cyclicals vs Defensives pair at all-time highs.

bullets.title: AVGO faces potential share loss at Google TPUv9 as MediaTek's Humufish gains traction — supply chain checks
bullets.body: JPMorgan Asia supply chain checks indicate MediaTek's Humufish (v9 TPU, N2 compute dies + HBM4e) is emerging as Google's primary v9 project, potentially displacing Broadcom at Google's next AI chip generation. This comes ahead of AVGO's earnings, where UBS had already cut its Anthropic ASIC contribution estimate from $21B to $8B in C2026 while raising its Meta XPU and OpenAI ramp estimates.

bullets.title: Chinese crude oil imports hit decade lows, adding supply-side pressure despite geopolitical oil spike
bullets.body: Chinese crude oil imports fell to their lowest level in a decade, reflecting weaker demand from the world's largest crude consumer. This structural demand headwind provides context against the near-term geopolitical price spike driven by Iran tensions and Strait of Hormuz risk.

bullets.title: Consumer credit cracks widen: personal savings at 2.6%, real wages negative YoY for first time since 2023
bullets.body: Personal savings collapsed to 2.6% in April, inflation reaccelerated to 3.8%, and real wages turned negative YoY for the first time since 2023 per Hedgeye. Weekly gas prices are up ~40% YoY. UBS cautions on low-end consumer while Goldman's prime brokerage book shows gross leverage at elevated levels, and upstream price pressures remain in the goods pipeline with further pass-through to consumers pending.
